messages:
Nora (People Ops): Quick policy pilot announcement: we're launching a 90-day Emergency Relocation & Family Stipend pilot. Purpose: support employees who must relocate suddenly for immediate family reasons (medical, caregiving, natural disaster). Pilot kicks off today. Details: up to 10 days paid relocation leave + one-time up to $2,000 temporary housing stipend (country-specific caps apply). Full FAQ & eligibility: https://redwood.company/hr/relocation-pilot :white_heart:
Cal (Prod): This is great. What counts as "immediate family"?
Nora (People Ops): Immediate family = spouse/partner, children, parents, legal guardians, siblings. We also allow household domestic partners where local law recognizes them.
Diego (Legal): We'll need some documentation for cross-border cases (immigration support, local regs). The checklist is in the FAQ. For privacy, employees can submit docs via our secure portal.
Hannah (Finance): Stipend payments are treated as non-reimbursable benefits in the payroll system (tax treatment varies by country). We'll provide gross-up options where required; reach out to payroll for country specifics.
Luis (EE): Is this compatible with short-term disability or parental leave? Example: relocation following urgent family care while on parental leave.
Nora (People Ops): Good Q. The relocation leave is distinct and can run concurrently with other leaves, but total paid time combined will be capped at 30 days in a rolling 12-month window. We'll coordinate with managers to avoid double-dipping.
Cal (Prod): How fast can someone get approved? In emergencies timing matters.
Nora (People Ops): We're aiming for same-day ack and 48-hour decision window for standard cases. For international/legal review that need extra checks, we'll target <5 business days. Submit via: https://redwood.company/forms/relocation-exception.
Benefits Bot: New Policy: Emergency Relocation & Family Stipend pilot live. Submit requests through the HR portal.
Diego (Legal): Cross-border note: for urgent relocations into or out of restricted countries we may need Security and Legal clearance before stipend is paid. We'll try to fast-track but flagging early helps.
Hannah (Finance): Receipts: temporary housing stipend can be advanced or reimbursed. If advanced, receipts required within 60 days. Fast-track reimbursements flagged as "priority" in the expense system.
Luis (EE): Any manager obligations? Approvals, blackout periods?
Nora (People Ops): Managers need to acknowledge requests within 24 hours and can raise business-critical flags (e.g., active sprint-critical roles). People Ops will adjudicate disputes. We also have a small reserve pool for coverage (ask Talent Ops).
Cal (Prod): Will contractors be eligible?
Nora (People Ops): Not part of the standard pilot. Contractors on payroll with specific agreements may be considered; talk to your recruiter/Manager.
Diego (Legal): Confidentiality is key. We'll redact sensitive details in approvals and only share what's necessary with Finance/Legal.
Hannah (Finance): Ops note: we'll publish a one-pager on tax implications per region next week. For immediate cases, ping payroll and include country in the form.
Cal (Prod): Amazing. Appreciate the quick rollout.
Nora (People Ops): Thanks all. We'll run the pilot for 90 days, monitor usage & feedback, then decide on permanent policy. Drop edge cases in #people-ops or DM me. :seedling:
